title: Electric Car and EV Basics
desc: Understand how electric vehicles work, charge, cost and stay safe, and how to advise buyers and fleets honestly.
outcomes: Explain motor, battery, charger and range.
Estimate running cost and charging time.
Judge battery health, safety and resale.
Write a buyer or fleet advice sheet.
task: Produce an advice sheet comparing one EV with one petrol car for a given user, with cost, range, charging and safety notes.
condition: A computer, public specifications, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. No high-voltage work is done.
standard: Maths is correct and in your currency; assumptions are stated; safety rules for high-voltage parts are included; claims are sourced; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Sales staff, drivers, fleet clerks, technician trainees.
evidence: comparison sheet, charging time sheet, safety notes, advice sheet
modules: Parts: battery pack, inverter, motor, charger, controller.
Energy use in kWh per 100 km.
A car using 15 kWh per 100 km travels 400 km on 60 kWh.
Range and life depend on the pack.
Capacity in kWh; usable capacity is less.
Heat, fast charging and deep discharge age batteries.
Warranty usually covers years and distance.
Keeping charge between 20% and 80% daily can slow ageing.
Slow home charging, faster wallbox, fast public chargers.
To add 30 kWh at 7 kW takes about 4.5 hours.
EV: kWh per 100 km times price per kWh.
Petrol: litres per 100 km times price per litre.
EV: 15 kWh x 8 INR = 120 INR per 100 km; petrol: 7 L x 100 INR = 700 INR.
Real range is not the label range.
Speed, temperature, load and hills change range.
Cold and highway driving cut range by 25%.
Orange cables are high voltage; only trained technicians work on them.
First responders need a rescue sheet.
A pack damage warning means stop and call the maker.
An old pack powers a shop's backup.
State fit: daily distance, home charging, budget.
List cons as well as pros.
Advice says an EV suits a commuter with home charging but not a user with no parking.
quiz: Returns some energy to the battery.
kWh per 100 km x price per kWh.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: car charging stations, portable charging, micro-mobility.
local: Standards, subsidies and tax differ by place.
ladder: L1: learner can name EV parts.
L3: learner can calculate charge times.
L6: learner can coordinate a fleet.
